targetText: The oldest Celtic laws which have been preserved show the gens still fully alive... in Scotland it was still in full strength in the middle of the eighteenth century, and here again it succumbed only to the weapons, laws, and courts of the English.
summary: Communal clan organization and shared land tenure survived among Celtic communities in Ireland and Scotland until destroyed by British military force and capitalist property laws.
context: Engels demonstrates that communal clan structures existed across Western Europe as well. In the Scottish Highlands, tribal clan solidarity resisted state centralization until suppressed following the 18th-century Jacobite uprisings.
